The notation $(f+g)(x)$ means the sum of the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x).$

**Method 1**

To evaluate $(f+g)(4),$ we find $f(4)$ and $g(4),$ and then add the results.

First, we find $f(4)$ and $g(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =2(4)+1=9 \\ g(4) & =-3(4)+5=-7\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we add the results:

$$
(f+g)(4)=f(4)+g(4)=9+(-7)=2
$$

**Method 2**

First, we find $(f+g)(x)$ by adding the two functions:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f+g)(x) & =(2x+1)+(-3x+5) \\  & =-x+6 \\  & =6-x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate $(f+g)(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}(f+g)(4) & =6-4=2\end{aligned}
$$

The notation $(fg)(x)$ means  the product of the functions  $f(x)$ and $g(x).$

**Method 1**

To evaluate $(fg)(3),$ we find $f(3)$ and $g(3),$ and then multiply the results.

First, we find $f(3)$ and $g(3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) & =(3)^{2}+1=10 \\ g(3) & =2(3)-1=5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we multiply the results:

$$
(fg)(3)=f(3)g(3)=10\cdot 5=50
$$

**Method 2**

First, we find $(fg)(x)$ by multiplying the two functions:

$$
\begin{aligned}(fg)(x) & =({x}^{2}+1)(2x-1) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+2x-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate $(fg)(3):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(fg)(3) & =2(3)^{3}-(3)^{2}+2(3)-1 \\  & =54-9+6-1 \\  & =50\end{aligned}
$$

To evaluate $(f/g)(3),$ we find $f(3)$ and $g(3),$ and then divide the results.

First, we find $f(3)$ and $g(3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) & =2(3)^{2}-6=12 \\ g(3) & =-2(3)+2=-4\end{aligned}

Now, we divide the results:

$$
(f/g)(3)=\frac{f(3)}{g(3)}=\frac{12}{-4}=-3
$$
